lectures.title: Drugs Used in Gynecology
lectures.framing: Every agent here does one of three things: disrupt the HPO axis, block the overgrowth of a sex-hormone-dependent tissue, or replace a hormone that is absent. Work out which, and the indications and adverse effects follow from it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The POC's primary mechanism is local, not central — that is the single most-tested fact here, and it is what makes adherence matter so much more for the mini-pill. Hypertension is relative; an active thromboembolic event is absolute, and it is absolute for combined methods only. Drospirenone is the anti-androgenic progestin (spironolactone-derived) — the one to reach for in hormonal acne, and the one that risks hyperkalemia; estranes and gonanes are androgenic instead. UPA beats LNG at every interval, including inside 72 hours ⚠ — an Elentra module question keys this the other way, and the lecture's own meta-analysis slide is the one to trust. GnRH agonists flare before they suppress; antagonists never flare. Finasteride lowers DHT, it does not block the androgen receptor — which is why it shrinks a prostate and thins body hair without touching muscle mass. ⚠ No emergency contraceptive works once implantation has happened — only mifepristone acts on an established pregnancy.

ER antagonist at hypothalamus + anterior pituitary, partial agonist at the ovary → removes negative feedback → ↑ GnRH and gonadotropins

blocks.html: The whole hormone story in one line: estrogen and progestin are opposing on the endometrium — estrogen proliferates (↑ endometrial cancer), progestin opposes it (protective), which is the only reason a progestin is added to an estrogen — but they are synergic on the breast, both driving proliferation, which is why adding a progestin does not fix the breast-cancer risk.

blocks.lead: Combined vs progestin-only — the contrast almost every question turns on
rows: breast cancer · undiagnosed bleeding · severe liver failure

blocks.lead: Emergency contraception — acts before implantation, by delaying ovulation and inhibiting follicular rupture.
rows: suppress the LH surge + direct ovarian action preventing follicle rupture
inflammatory uterine environment; copper toxic to sperm and blastocyst

blocks.html: Benefits of hormonal contraception — ↓ ovarian cysts · ↓ ovarian and endometrial cancer · ↓ PID · ↓ dysmenorrhea · ↓ endometriosis · lighter, predictable periods · improved acne and PMS. Weigh these against the risks of pregnancy itself, not against zero.

Contraindications to hormonal contraception — breast or reproductive-tract cancer · history of stroke/thromboembolic disease/MI/CAD · severe cirrhosis or liver tumour · undiagnosed abnormal bleeding · ⚠ hypertension is the only RELATIVE one on the list · caution if smoker >35 years.
